claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 079 (Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation.; papers: Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation; Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/079.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.
October thm:local-smoothing: for n>=2, 2<=p<infinity and epsilon>0, the L^p spacetime norm on [1,2] of exp(-iT|D|)f is bounded by the L^p norm of J^(max(0,(n-1)/2-n/p)+epsilon)f; epsilon=0 at p=2.
October prop:current and eq:regularized-current give A>=0 with divergence-free real columns, mu=A_TT>0, A:H(lambda|Phi|^2)=0, and a regularizing cofactor with zero full-normal flux.
October lem:cofactor-divergence: for k=3 or 4 slots and any smooth real u, sum_(a,alpha) conjugate(e_alpha) partial_(a,alpha) C(H(u))_(ab)=0, including indefinite and singular Hessians.
October lem:fiber-geometry: for r=|W|^2/w0^2+100|Phi/a|^2-1, H_fib(r)>0 and H(r)>=0 has one quaternionic null line contained in G(r)^perp and ker H(|Phi|^2).
For each fixed admissible a,h,lambda, the October fiber equation det H_fib(B0+u)=lambda mu, H_fib(B0+u)>0, u=0 on the wall has a unique smooth solution with smooth parameter dependence and u<=0.
October prop:energy-flux: Delta_z F(z)+integral_(Omega_z) A:Sigma d zeta = integral rho G(r)^* A_w G(r) delta(r) d zeta, where F=E_z(u)+integral(-u)mu, rho=(u/r)|wall, and G(r) is the full gradient.
October prop:fixed-barrier supplies wavelength-uniform upper and lower bounds for the determinant energy at its two prescribed circles, and an exponentially small lateral wave-flux bound.
October prop:periodic-cap: cap-supported annular torus data obey the critical p_c=2n/(n-1) spacetime bound C[log(2/h)]^(2/p_c) times their initial L^p_c norm, uniformly in h and cap direction.
October Section transfer passes from the periodic cap estimate to Euclidean annuli and the claimed Sobolev range by angular decomposition, interpolation, and frequency summation.
September thm:main: for every epsilon>0, ||Uf||_(L^3(R^3 x [1,2])) <= C_epsilon ||J^epsilon f||_(L^3(R^3)).
September thm:cylinder and the canonical-name interior and action inequalities bound the cylinder model growth exponents. This is a separate, unaudited analytic route.
September thm:round: for every 0<eta<1 the classical and wave round-cone growth exponents are at most 100 eta, with the stated finite contractions and Hilbert multiplicity.

September prop:phys-annular: for every delta>0, ||W_H g||_(L^3(R^3 x [1,2])) <= C_delta H^(-delta)||g||_3, with uniform annular multiplier bounds; initial regularity and terminal synthesis are required.

Dimension-independent moving-wall defect formula: for smooth Dirichlet u with det D_u=lambda mu and conserved positive A orthogonal to the background, Delta F+integral A:Sigma equals the full current flux minus lambda^(-1) integral rho integral_0^1 G(r)^*C(H(B0+theta u))G(r) dtheta delta(r). If B=H(B0)>=0 and H(r)>=0, this defect is nonnegative; at rho>0 it vanishes exactly when ker B intersect ker H(r) intersect G(r)^perp is nonzero. The actual October fiber satisfies this condition.

For every finite quaternionic dimension, if Bq=Rq=0, nu^*q=0, and K=B+tR+nu w^*+w nu^*, then every v with v^*nu=0 satisfies v^*Kq=0. Together with q!=0 this makes the compression of K to nu^perp singular. The October holomorphic fiber has the explicit null vector (1,W,-sum W_j^2/2) in null coordinates, in every dimension.
For each fixed admissible a,h,lambda, the October fiber equation det H_fib(B0+u)=lambda mu, H_fib(B0+u)>0, u=0 on the wall has a unique smooth solution with smooth parameter dependence and u<=0.

external_assumptions.statement: Smooth solvability on a flat quaternionic quotient with a smooth strict subsolution; the periodic three-slot reduction, locally uniform barriers, and smooth finite-dimensional parameter dependence recover October Theorem A.1.
external_assumptions.source: Ma and Zhu, The Dirichlet problem for quaternionic Monge-Ampere equations on flat quaternionic quotients

claims.natural_statement: For every finite index type and genuine real quaternions, Bq=Rq=0, nu^*q=0, and v^*nu=0 imply v^*(B+tR+nu w^*+w nu^*)q=0 for every real t. In every finite transverse complex dimension, (1,W,-sum W_j^2/2) is a nonzero common null vector of Y dW and dPhi, and det [[I,-W],[W^t,1-sum W_j^2/2]]=1+sum W_j^2/2, nonzero when abs(sum W_j^2)<2. These are the algebraic subclaims, not the analytic PDE theorem.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace EnergyBridge

abbrev Q := Quaternion ℝ

section QuaternionicWall

variable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]

def pair (v w : ι → Q) : Q := ∑ i, star (v i) * w i

def act (B : ι → ι → Q) (q : ι → Q) : ι → Q :=
  fun i => ∑ j, B i j * q j

def wall (B R : ι → ι → Q) (ν w : ι → Q) (t : ℝ) : ι → ι → Q :=
  fun i j => B i j + (t : Q) * R i j + ν i * star (w j) + w i * star (ν j)

theorem pair_right_mul (v w : ι → Q) (a : Q) :
    pair v (fun i => w i * a) = pair v w * a := by
  simp [pair, Finset.sum_mul, mul_assoc]

theorem act_wall (B R : ι → ι → Q) (ν w q : ι → Q) (t : ℝ) :
    act (wall B R ν w t) q =
      fun i => act B q i + (t : Q) * act R q i +
        ν i * pair w q + w i * pair ν q := by
  funext i
  simp [act, wall, pair, add_mul, mul_assoc, Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]

theorem boundary_null_pairing
    (B R : ι → ι → Q) (ν w q v : ι → Q) (t : ℝ)
    (hB : act B q = 0) (hR : act R q = 0)
    (hνq : pair ν q = 0) (hvν : pair v ν = 0) :
    pair v (act (wall B R ν w t) q) = 0 := by
  have hk : act (wall B R ν w t) q = fun i => ν i * pair w q := by
    rw [act_wall, hB, hR, hνq]
    simp
  rw [hk, pair_right_mul, hvν, zero_mul]

end QuaternionicWall

section HolomorphicFiber

variable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]

def squareSum (W : ι → ℂ) : ℂ := ∑ i, W i * W i

def ratioDifferential (W : ι → ℂ) (y : ℂ) (p : ι → ℂ) : ι → ℂ :=
  fun i => p i - W i * y

def passiveDifferential (W : ι → ℂ) (y : ℂ) (p : ι → ℂ) (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  -(squareSum W) / 2 * y + (∑ i, W i * p i) + s

theorem fiber_null_vector (W : ι → ℂ) :
    ratioDifferential W 1 W = 0 ∧
      passiveDifferential W 1 W (-(squareSum W) / 2) = 0 := by
  constructor
  · funext i
    simp [ratioDifferential]
  · simp only [passiveDifferential, mul_one, ← squareSum]
    ring

theorem null_vector_nonzero (W : ι → ℂ) :
    (1, W, -(squareSum W) / 2) ≠ (0, 0, 0) := by
  intro h
  have hfirst : (1 : ℂ) = 0 := congrArg Prod.fst h
  exact one_ne_zero hfirst

variable [DecidableEq ι]

def scaledSpatialJacobian (W : ι → ℂ) : Matrix (ι ⊕ Unit) (ι ⊕ Unit) ℂ :=
  Matrix.fromBlocks 1 (fun i _ => -W i) (fun _ j => W j)
    (fun _ _ => 1 - squareSum W / 2)

theorem scaled_spatial_jacobian_det (W : ι → ℂ) :
    (scaledSpatialJacobian W).det = 1 + squareSum W / 2 := by
  rw [scaledSpatialJacobian, Matrix.det_fromBlocks_one₁₁]
  simp [Matrix.det_unique, Matrix.sub_apply, Matrix.mul_apply, squareSum,
    mul_neg, Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
  ring

theorem chart_denominator_nonzero (S : ℂ) (hS : ‖S‖ < 2) :
    1 + S / 2 ≠ 0 := by
  intro h
  have hs : S = -2 := by
    linear_combination 2 * h
  rw [hs] at hS
  norm_num at hS

end HolomorphicFiber

section RealCompression

variable {κ : Type*} [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]

theorem real_compression_singular (M : Matrix κ κ ℝ) (q : κ → ℝ)
    (hq : q ≠ 0) (hMq : M *ᵥ q = 0) : M.det = 0 := by
  exact Matrix.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_iff.mp ⟨q, hq, hMq⟩

end RealCompression

end EnergyBridge

claims.natural_statement: Dimension-independent moving-wall defect theorem: assume smooth u<=0 with zero lateral boundary values, smooth conserved A>=0 with mu=A_TT>0, B=H(B0)>=0, det B=0, A:B=0, lambda>0 constant, and D_u=H_fib(B0+u)>0 with det D_u=lambda mu. Then Delta F+integral A:Sigma equals the full current flux minus lambda^(-1) integral rho integral_0^1 G(r)^*C(H(B0+theta u))G(r) dtheta delta(r). If H(r)>=0 on the wall, this defect is nonnegative; at every boundary point with rho>0 its density vanishes exactly when ker B intersect ker H(r) intersect G(r)^perp is nonzero. The actual October fiber satisfies this condition and its regularizing current has zero flux.

For every finite index type and genuine real quaternions, Bq=Rq=0, nu^*q=0, and v^*nu=0 imply v^*(B+tR+nu w^*+w nu^*)q=0 for every real t. In every finite transverse complex dimension, (1,W,-sum W_j^2/2) is a nonzero common null vector of Y dW and dPhi, and det [[I,-W],[W^t,1-sum W_j^2/2]]=1+sum W_j^2/2, nonzero when abs(sum W_j^2)<2. These are the algebraic subclaims, not the analytic PDE theorem.

routes.retired_because: The goal was restated before evidence to make det B=0 and u<=0 explicit; the old goal-version reference must not inherit evidence. The same mathematical route continues as R_ENERGY_CHARACTERISTIC_WALL_V2.

The exact moving-wall defect vanishes on the actual October fibers: k=(1,W,-sum W_j^2/2) is in ker H(r) intersect ker H(B0) intersect G(r)^perp. Hence an omitted cofactor wall contribution cannot refute prop:energy-flux. This does not exclude errors in downstream scale estimates or the independent September argument.
